calibracao: O vídeo mostra o réu dando um segundo soco depois que a vítima recuou com as mãos baixas, mas não mostra os 2–3 s anteriores ao primeiro soco, quando a defesa alega que a vítima empurrou o réu contra um carro.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 31, a retail store manager, is charged with assault after a fight outside a sports bar at about 11:40 p.m. The complainant suffered a broken nose and needed six stitches above the left eye.

A security camera above the bar entrance shows {NAME} striking the complainant in the face. The complainant then steps back with both hands lowered, and about two seconds later {NAME} steps forward and strikes a second time. The camera does not cover the two or three seconds before the first punch, because both people stepped partly out of frame. The bouncer testified that the two had argued inside over a spilled drink and that {NAME} said "this isn't over" on the way out.

{NAME} testified that the complainant followed {him} outside, shouted threats, and shoved {him} hard against a parked car, that {he} punched to get free, and that {he} still felt threatened when {he} threw the second punch. Responding officers noted no marks on {NAME} and no damage to the parked car. The complainant testified to being punched without warning while walking to a car.

calibracao: A identificação depende de uma única testemunha a 15 m, à noite, com "80% de certeza"; a capa do celular da vítima apareceu na lixeira atrás do prédio do réu, que tem 48 apartamentos.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 26, a bank loan officer, is charged with assault for a beating at a bus stop at around 10:15 p.m. The complainant suffered a fractured wrist and bruised ribs and could not describe the attacker, who wore a dark jacket with the hood up. The attacker took the complainant's phone.

A food truck worker about 15 meters away watched the attack under a streetlight. Four days later, the worker picked {NAME} out of a six-photo lineup and told the detective, "I'm pretty sure, maybe 80 percent." The next morning, a building manager found the complainant's phone case, with the complainant's ID card still inside, in a trash bin behind the apartment building where {NAME} lives. The building has 48 units, and the bus stop is about a 12-minute walk away.

{NAME} testified that {he} was at home all evening. Phone records show no activity on {NAME}'s phone between 9:40 p.m. and 10:45 p.m. {His} roommate testified that {NAME} was home but admitted to falling asleep at around 10:00 p.m.

calibracao: O réu admite o empurrão e alega legítima defesa contra um golpe com garrafa que nunca foi encontrada; o atendente viu, só de relance e pelo reflexo da vitrine, a vítima já se virando quando foi empurrada.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 38, a city bus driver, is charged with assault after a confrontation in a convenience store parking lot. The complainant suffered a concussion and a cut on the scalp that required staples.

{NAME} admits pushing the complainant, who fell and hit the curb. {He} testified that the two had a short argument about a parking space, and that the complainant then grabbed a glass bottle from a trash bin and swung it at {his} head. {NAME} said {he} pushed the complainant away to avoid being hit.

No bottle was recovered, and officers found no broken glass near the spot where the complainant fell. The store clerk testified to glancing at the lot in the reflection of the front window and seeing the complainant "already turning toward their car" when {NAME} pushed with both hands. The clerk admitted that the glimpse lasted about a second and that posters covered part of the window. The complainant denied picking up anything and said {NAME} came at them from behind.

{NAME} called 911 right after the fall and stayed at the scene until police arrived.

calibracao: Testemunhas opostas, cada uma ligada a uma das partes; o laudo médico é compatível tanto com golpe quanto com bloqueio; a mensagem do réu é ambígua.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 29, a line cook, is charged with assault after a fight in the kitchen of the restaurant where {he} worked. The complainant, a coworker, suffered a deep bruise on the forearm and a sprained shoulder.

The complainant testified that {NAME} became angry over an order mix-up and struck them twice with a metal ladle. A dishwasher, who is a close friend of the complainant, supported that version. A second cook, who carpools with {NAME}, testified that the complainant grabbed {NAME}'s collar first and that {NAME} raised the ladle only to block.

The emergency physician testified that the forearm bruise could come either from a blow or from a defensive block against a held object. The kitchen camera was broken that week.

Text messages show that {NAME} wrote to a friend that night: "I lost it at work, I really messed up." {NAME} testified that the message referred to yelling during the argument, not to hitting anyone.

calibracao: O DNA sob as unhas da vítima pode vir da briga gravada ao meio-dia; um vizinho viu o carro do réu na entrada "por volta das 7", quando o réu diz que ainda não tinha voltado, mas não tem certeza do horário.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 34, an insurance claims adjuster, is charged with assault after a neighbor was found injured in the shared driveway of a duplex at about 7:00 p.m. The complainant suffered a fractured cheekbone and could not identify the attacker, saying they were struck from behind.

Material under the complainant's fingernails contained {NAME}'s DNA. The two had a long-running dispute about parking, and a third neighbor recorded a phone video at about 1:00 p.m. that day showing the two pushing and grabbing each other for about ten seconds before separating.

{NAME} testified that {he} left for a client inspection at 3:00 p.m. and returned after 8:00 p.m. The client confirmed that {NAME} left the inspection site at about 6:15 p.m.; the drive back takes about 35 minutes. A neighbor across the street testified to seeing {NAME}'s car parked in the driveway "around seven, maybe a little before or after," while taking out the trash, and could not be more precise. A wooden board with traces of the complainant's blood was found by the driveway, without usable fingerprints.

calibracao: O réu admite o soco e alega defesa de um amigo, que confirma a versão em juízo; mas no dia seguinte o amigo escreveu ao réu "they were just yelling, you didn't need to swing", e agora diz que se referia a outra discussão.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 27, a hotel front desk clerk, is charged with assault after punching a stranger at a late-night food stand. The complainant lost a tooth and suffered a cut lip.

{NAME} admits throwing one punch. {He} testified that the complainant was standing very close to {his} friend, yelling, and had pulled back a fist, and that {he} struck first to stop what {he} believed was an imminent attack on the friend. The friend testified to the same account.

The complainant testified to complaining about the friend cutting in line and said there was no raised fist. The vendor testified that the complainant was "loud and in the friend's face" but could not see the complainant's hands because of the counter. The next morning, the friend texted {NAME}: "they were just yelling, you didn't need to swing." At trial, the friend said the message was about a different argument earlier that night, which no one else saw.

A phone video taken by a customer begins just after the punch and shows the complainant on the ground and {NAME} stepping back.

calibracao: A vítima reconhece o réu com segurança, mas os dois têm um litígio que dá motivo para uma falsa acusação; na véspera, o réu mandou à vítima "You'll regret this lawsuit", que diz se referir aos custos do processo.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 42, a real estate agent, is charged with assault after a former business partner was attacked in a parking garage at 9:20 p.m. The complainant suffered a broken arm.

The complainant testified to recognizing {NAME} clearly in the garage lights, from about two meters away, and to being hit with a metal pipe. The two had run a small property management business together until it closed eight months earlier, and the complainant was suing {NAME} over unpaid debts. The garage cameras were not recording that night due to a power issue. No pipe was recovered.

The day before the attack, {NAME} sent the complainant a text message: "You'll regret this lawsuit." {NAME} testified that {he} meant the legal costs the complainant would face, not violence.

A parking attendant saw a person in a gray rain jacket leave the garage on foot right after the attack but did not see the face. {NAME} owns a gray rain jacket. {NAME} testified that {he} was at home alone watching television. {His} phone shows no activity between 8:00 p.m. and 10:30 p.m., and {his} home is about 20 minutes from the garage.

calibracao: A vítima estava muito embriagada, mudou a versão e outros convidados vestiam verde; o réu discutiu com a vítima junto à escada e pediu um ride-share minutos depois da hora estimada da queda, que é incerta.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 24, a college student who works part-time at a grocery store, is charged with assault after a house party. The complainant was found in the backyard with bruises on the face and a cracked rib.

At the hospital, the complainant told officers that "the person in the green shirt" pushed them down the back steps and kicked them. {NAME} was wearing a green shirt that night. Two other guests also wore green, according to party photos. At trial, the complainant said {NAME} punched them before the fall, a detail not in the first statement. The complainant's blood alcohol level was 0.19.

Another guest testified to seeing {NAME} and the complainant arguing on the porch, next to the back steps, shortly before the complainant was found. {NAME} admits the argument, about a borrowed speaker, but says {he} went back inside and left soon after. A ride-share receipt shows {NAME} requested a ride three minutes after the time a guest estimated the fall happened, and was picked up at the front door. The guest who found the complainant said the estimate could be off by ten minutes either way.

calibracao: Confissão vaga após 4 h de interrogatório, sob efeito de sedativo e com um detalhe errado (a ponte); as outras provas são a roupa e a presença perto da trilha.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 36, a hospital lab technician, is charged with assault after a stranger was beaten on a jogging trail early in the morning. The complainant suffered a fractured jaw and described the attacker only as a person in a gray sweatshirt.

{NAME} was stopped near the trail about an hour later, wearing a gray sweatshirt. In a recorded police interview that lasted four hours, {NAME} eventually said, "Fine, maybe I hit someone, I don't remember." Medical records show {he} had taken a prescribed sedative the night before. {He} had waived the right to a lawyer in writing.

In the interview, {NAME} said the fight happened "by the bridge," but the attack took place about 800 meters from the bridge. A trail camera captured a person in a gray sweatshirt running away from the area, but the image is too blurry to show the face.

{NAME} testified that {he} walks the trail daily after night shifts and that {he} only agreed with the detectives so the interview would end.

calibracao: O réu alega que reagiu a uma tentativa de roubo, e a carteira no chão apoia essa versão; o vídeo mostra golpes enquanto a vítima cobria a cabeça, sem deixar claro se ela ainda resistia.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 45, a property manager, is charged with assault after a confrontation near an ATM. The complainant suffered two broken ribs and facial bruises.

{NAME} testified that the complainant approached {him} at the ATM, demanded money, and grabbed {his} wallet, and that {he} wrestled the complainant to the ground and held them there until the threat ended. The complainant denies demanding anything and testified to asking {NAME} only for directions.

A bank camera shows the two struggling. The footage shows {NAME} on top of the complainant, delivering at least three blows while the complainant appears to be covering their head. The camera has no audio. {NAME}'s wallet was found on the ground about a meter away. A passerby who called 911 testified to hearing someone yell "give it back" but could not say who yelled it.

{NAME} testified that {he} could not tell whether the complainant had stopped resisting and that {he} feared the complainant had a weapon. No weapon was found.

calibracao: O autoatendimento tinha histórico de falhas de leitura; mas os três itens não pagos são os mais caros do carrinho, e o réu não olhou a tela nenhuma vez.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 33, an insurance agent, is charged with retail theft after leaving a home improvement store with merchandise worth $612 that had not been paid for.

{NAME} used a self-checkout station to buy 14 items. The receipt shows payment for 11 items totaling $96. The three unpaid items were a cordless drill, a battery pack, and a set of drill bits, the most expensive items in the cart. A loss prevention officer watched the transaction on camera and stopped {NAME} past the exit doors.

The store's maintenance log shows that this station had 23 recorded scanning errors in the previous month, including items that beeped but did not register. The video shows {NAME} passing the drill over the scanner, but the screen is not visible. The officer testified that {NAME} "did not look at the screen once."

{NAME} testified that {he} did not notice the missing items and offered to pay when stopped.

calibracao: O vídeo não mostra o rosto e o réu diz que empresta o cartão de fidelidade e a mochila; a mochila do vídeo tem um remendo igual ao da mochila do réu, e o celular do réu buscou o preço de revenda do modelo naquela noite.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 28, a bartender, is charged with retail theft for taking two pairs of wireless headphones worth $698 from an electronics store.

Security video shows a person in a gray baseball cap placing the headphones inside a backpack and leaving without paying at 4:12 p.m. The video is low resolution, and the face is hidden by the cap. Twenty minutes earlier, the same person bought a phone charger at the register and scanned a loyalty card registered to {NAME}.

The backpack in the video has a red rectangular patch on the front pocket. Police seized a backpack from {NAME}'s apartment with a similar red patch, which {NAME} says {he} sewed on {himself}; patches of that style are sold widely online. At 9:30 p.m. that evening, {NAME}'s phone searched for the resale price of the exact headphone model. No headphones were found in the apartment.

{NAME} testified that {he} often lets friends use {his} loyalty card number for discounts, that friends sometimes borrow the backpack, and that {he} looked up the price because {he} was thinking of buying the same headphones.

calibracao: O réu tirou as etiquetas de segurança e saiu com os casacos; o ponto disputado é o valor: o desconto de 30% era só para membros do programa de fidelidade, mas a placa era ambígua.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 40, a high school teacher, is charged with retail theft of merchandise worth over $500 from a department store.

A store detective saw {NAME} remove the security tags from two winter coats in a fitting room and leave the store wearing one coat and carrying the other in a shopping bag. {NAME} was stopped outside with both coats. The ticket price on each coat was $265, for a total of $530.

That weekend, a sign on the coat rack read "30% off all outerwear" in large letters and, in small print at the bottom, "for loyalty members, at the register." {NAME} is not a loyalty member. At the member price, the total would have been $371. The store manager testified that non-members always pay the ticket price.

{NAME} does not deny leaving with the coats. {He} testified that {he} meant to pay at a register on another floor and forgot because {he} was on a phone call. The removed tags were found in the fitting room trash can.

calibracao: Os itens estavam na sacola do réu, mas um conhecido com antecedentes, que fugiu, pode tê-los posto ali; a perícia mostra o celular do réu bloqueado nos 40 s em que o réu diz que o estava olhando.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 23, a part-time grocery store clerk, is charged with retail theft of vitamins and electric toothbrushes worth $544 from a drugstore.

{NAME} entered the store with an acquaintance. A camera shows the two walking together through the health products aisle, where the acquaintance's back blocks the view of the shelves for about 40 seconds. After the alarm sounded at the exit, a store employee found the merchandise in a tote bag carried by {NAME}. The acquaintance ran away and was never charged.

{NAME} testified that {he} did not know the items were in {his} bag and that the acquaintance had asked to "put something" in it while {he} was looking at {his} phone. A forensic report on {NAME}'s phone shows that the screen was locked during those 40 seconds. {NAME} said {he} may have been reading notifications on the lock screen. The employee testified that, when the alarm went off, {NAME} said, "Please don't call the police."

The acquaintance has two prior shoplifting convictions and could not be found to testify.

calibracao: O anúncio foi criado com o e-mail do réu e as fotos foram tiradas na cozinha do réu; mas a conta também foi acessada de outro aparelho, e o réu diz que um hóspede que alugava um quarto no apartamento usou a conta.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 35, a real estate agent, is charged with retail theft for taking four smart home cameras worth $760 from a big-box store.

Store video shows a person in a gray rain jacket and sunglasses taking the cameras from a shelf and leaving through the garden center exit without paying. The face is not clearly visible. Two days later, four cameras of the same model, still sealed, were listed for sale on an online marketplace. The listing account was created with {NAME}'s email address, and the listing photos were taken on a kitchen counter that matches the one in {NAME}'s apartment. {NAME} admits owning a gray rain jacket.

Marketplace records show that the account was accessed from two phones, one of which belongs to {NAME}. The other phone was never identified.

{NAME} testified that a short-term guest renting a room in {his} apartment that week must have used {his} account to list the cameras. {NAME} could not provide the guest's full name, and the booking was paid in cash.

calibracao: A TV no rack inferior não foi paga; o vídeo mostra o réu pondo as toalhas de papel sobre a caixa da TV pouco antes do caixa, e o caixa acha que o réu respondeu "no"; pode ter sido arrumação do carrinho e o caixa repete a pergunta dezenas de vezes por hora.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 46, a postal carrier, is charged with retail theft for leaving a warehouse club with a television worth $649 that had not been paid for.

{NAME} went through a staffed checkout with a full cart. The cashier scanned 31 items worth $287, but the television, in a large box on the lower rack of the cart, was not scanned. At the exit, the receipt checker noticed the box and stopped {NAME}.

The checkout line video shows that, about a minute before reaching the cashier, {NAME} took a bulky pack of paper towels from the top of the cart and placed it on the lower rack, partly covering the television box. The cashier testified to asking, as usual, "anything on the bottom?" and believes {NAME} answered "no," but admitted to asking that question dozens of times an hour. The video has no audio.

{NAME} testified that {he} moved the paper towels to make room for other items on top and that {he} did not hear the question in the noisy checkout area. {He} paid with a membership card in {his} own name.

calibracao: O fiscal perdeu o réu de vista por um minuto, e o vídeo não mostra quem abriu a porta lateral; não havia prateleira no corredor onde o réu diz ter deixado as garrafas.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 30, a pharmacist, is charged with retail theft for taking three bottles of premium wine worth $540 from a supermarket.

A loss prevention officer testified to watching {NAME} put the three bottles into a large shoulder bag in the wine aisle. The officer followed {NAME} but lost sight of {him} for about one minute when {NAME} turned into a hallway leading to the restrooms and to a side door to the parking lot. {NAME} then walked out through the main exit without paying for anything. The officer stopped {him} in the parking lot and searched the bag, which contained no wine. Thirty minutes later, staff found the three bottles behind a planter just outside the side door.

The hallway camera shows {NAME} entering and leaving the hallway; it also shows the side door opening once during that minute, but a stack of boxes blocks the view of who opened it.

{NAME} testified that {he} changed {his} mind about the wine and left the bottles on a shelf in the hallway, and that someone else must have carried them outside. The officer testified that there is no shelf in that hallway; {NAME} then said {he} may have set them on the stack of boxes.

calibracao: O réu diz que fazia a devolução a pedido de um conhecido, sem saber que as botas eram furtadas, e a câmera não mostra o réu tirando as caixas da prateleira; o recibo era de outra pessoa.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 27, a call center representative, is charged with retail theft for a return scheme at a sporting goods store. Prosecutors say {NAME} took two pairs of hiking boots from the shelves, then "returned" them at the service desk using an old receipt, receiving $520 in store credit.

Video shows {NAME} entering the store with a folded shopping bag, walking to the footwear section, and going to the service desk with two boxes of boots about ten minutes later. The footwear camera shows {NAME} near the boot shelves but does not show {him} removing boxes. The receipt {NAME} used came from a purchase made three weeks earlier with a credit card that does not belong to {him}.

{NAME} testified that an acquaintance handed {him} the receipt and the boots in the parking lot and promised to split the credit. {He} said {he} walked to the footwear section only to compare prices. Phone records show several calls between {NAME} and an unregistered number that morning.

calibracao: O crachá do réu abriu o depósito; o réu diz que o perdeu dois dias antes, mas o único registro do aviso é posterior ao furto; naquela tarde, o réu perguntou a um colega se a câmera do depósito ainda apontava para a doca. O código do alarme era conhecido por quatro pessoas.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 37, an assistant store manager, is charged with retail theft for removing two laptops worth $1,480 from the stockroom of the electronics store where {he} worked.

The store's access system shows that {NAME}'s badge opened the stockroom at 9:52 p.m., after closing. Inventory counted the next morning was short two laptops. The stockroom camera was pointed at the loading dock and did not show the shelves. The rear door alarm was turned off with the manager code, which is known to four employees, including {NAME}.

A sales associate testified that, that afternoon, {NAME} asked whether the stockroom camera "still points at the dock." {NAME} testified that {he} asked because {he} had suggested moving the camera weeks earlier.

{NAME} testified that {he} lost {his} badge two days before the theft and told the store manager in person. The store manager says the only report was a text message sent the morning after the theft. No laptops were found.

calibracao: A vendedora diz ter visto o rosto e reconheceu o réu minutos depois, mas num reconhecimento show-up, sugestivo, em que o réu era o único do grupo de jaqueta verde, e outros clientes vestiam verde; os óculos estavam numa lixeira a 10 m da mesa do grupo.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 22, a university student, is charged with retail theft of sunglasses worth $585 from a boutique in a shopping mall.

A sales associate testified to seeing a customer in a green jacket slip four pairs of designer sunglasses into a coat pocket while the associate was helping another customer, and to seeing the customer's face clearly for a few seconds. The customer left with a group of four people. About five minutes later, mall security brought the associate to the food court, pointed out the group, and asked whether the person was there. The associate immediately pointed to {NAME}, the only person in the group wearing a green jacket. The four pairs of sunglasses were found in a trash can about ten meters from the group's table.

The associate admitted that two other customers in the store that afternoon also wore green. The boutique camera was not recording because of a system update. No sunglasses were found on {NAME} or on any other member of the group.

{NAME} testified that {he} was in the boutique only briefly and never touched the sunglasses.

calibracao: As digitais do réu na janela arrombada podem vir da vistoria do seguro; mas estão na face interna do caixilho, e o laudo assinado pelo réu registra só inspeção externa; o réu diz que abriu a janela para checar a vedação.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 32, an insurance appraiser, is charged with residential burglary of a detached house. While the owners were away for a weekend, someone forced open a rear window and took jewelry, a laptop, and about $800 in cash.

Investigators lifted two fingerprints from the inside surface of the forced window frame, the side facing the room. Both matched {NAME}. Fresh pry marks on the outside of the frame matched a flat screwdriver, a common tool. About five weeks earlier, {NAME} had inspected storm damage to the rear windows for the owners' insurance company. The inspection report, signed by {NAME}, describes an "exterior inspection only."

The owners testified that they did not let anyone into the house during the inspection and did not see the inspector open any window. A fingerprint expert testified that prints on a painted frame can last for weeks and that their age cannot be determined.

{NAME} testified that {he} opened the window from outside to check the seal, which would have meant touching the inner surface, and that {he} did not record it because it was routine. {His} roommate confirmed that {NAME} was home Saturday evening but away Sunday afternoon, when the neighbors believe the burglary happened.

calibracao: O réu vendeu o relógio furtado com documento próprio dois dias depois e diz que o comprou de um desconhecido; não há vestígio no apartamento, e o celular do réu ficou desligado durante quase toda a janela do furto, algo que não ocorreu em nenhum outro dia do mês.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 29, a restaurant shift manager, is charged with residential burglary of an apartment from which a gold watch, two rings, and a tablet were taken between 1:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m.

Two days after the burglary, {NAME} sold the gold watch to a pawn shop, showing {his} own driver's license and signing the receipt. The watch had a unique engraving that the owner described before it was recovered. Its market value is about $1,200. The other items were never found.

{NAME} testified that {he} bought the watch for $150 from a stranger at a gas station and sold it to the pawn shop for $400 the same week. {He} could not give the stranger's name or a clear description. The gas station's cameras keep footage for only 24 hours.

There were no fingerprints, shoe prints, or DNA linking {NAME} to the apartment. Phone company records show that {NAME}'s phone was switched off from 12:40 p.m. to 4:25 p.m. that day, the only time it was off that month. {NAME} said the battery died. {He} lives about 15 minutes from the apartment.

calibracao: A pegada é de um tênis muito vendido e o celular do réu estava na área, onde mora um amigo, cujo álibi tem uma lacuna; nenhum objeto furtado foi encontrado.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 25, a junior accountant, is charged with residential burglary of a townhouse. Someone kicked in the back door on a weekday morning and took two laptops and a gaming console. The owners were at work from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. that day.

Investigators photographed a muddy shoe print on the kitchen floor. The print matches the sole pattern and size of a running shoe found in {NAME}'s closet. A shoe expert testified that the model is one of the best-selling running shoes in the country.

Cell tower data place {NAME}'s phone in the area of the townhouse between 9:00 and 11:30 a.m. {NAME}'s friend lives about four blocks away and testified that {NAME} came over that morning to help move furniture, but left "for a while" at some point; the friend could not say when or for how long. None of the stolen items were found.

calibracao: O DNA do réu numa bituca no pátio pode vir de visitas quando o réu era vizinho; mas o laboratório diz que o DNA está pouco degradado, "mais compatível com dias que com meses", sem datação precisa; o réu tinha conhecimento da coleção e dificuldades financeiras.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 38, a sales representative, is charged with residential burglary of a house. Someone broke a glass panel in the back door and stole a coin collection worth about $9,000.

A cigarette butt found on the back patio, about two meters from the broken door, contained {NAME}'s DNA. {NAME} lived in the house next door until three months before the burglary and sometimes smoked on the homeowners' patio during backyard gatherings. A lab analyst testified that the DNA showed little degradation, "more consistent with days than with months" outdoors, but that the age of a sample cannot be determined with certainty. It had rained twice in the week before the burglary.

The homeowners had shown the coin collection to several visitors over the years, including {NAME}. A neighbor's camera recorded a car similar to {NAME}'s, a common silver sedan, passing on the street 40 minutes before the estimated time of the burglary. The plate is not readable.

{NAME} testified that {he} was at {his} new apartment that evening. {He} has no witnesses. Bank records show that {NAME} had fallen behind on rent and had received an eviction warning the week before.

calibracao: A entrada foi com chave; o réu não devolveu a cópia, mas outras duas pessoas também tinham chave; há mensagem ameaçadora e um depósito de US$ 1.400 em espécie dois dias depois, que o réu atribui à venda de móveis, com comprovação parcial.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 27, a graphic designer, is charged with residential burglary of an apartment {he} used to share with the complainant. Three months after {NAME} moved out, someone entered the apartment while it was empty and took a camera, two lenses, and an envelope with $1,500 in cash.

There was no forced entry. {NAME} admits never returning {his} key. The complainant testified that two other people also had keys: a dog walker and a former partner of the complainant. Both testified that they did not enter the apartment that day.

The complainant testified that {NAME} knew where the cash envelope was kept. A text message from {NAME}, sent two weeks before the burglary, says: "You still owe me for the last two months of utilities, and I'm going to get it one way or another." Two days after the burglary, {NAME} deposited $1,400 in cash into {his} bank account.

{NAME} testified that the message was about filing a small claims case and that the cash came from selling furniture to buyers {he} found online; {he} produced one listing for a sofa priced at $300. {NAME} says {he} was working alone at home that afternoon.

calibracao: O réu foi achado de madrugada dentro da garagem anexa, com luvas e lanterna, e diz que procurava um gato perdido (há post às 1:50); mas o morador viu a pessoa mexendo no trinco por um minuto e há arranhões de aparência recente no trinco, que não se sabe se são antigos.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 34, a hospital pharmacist who works night shifts, is charged with residential burglary after being found at about 3:30 a.m. inside the attached garage of a house two blocks from {his} own home. Under state law, an attached garage is part of the dwelling.

The homeowner heard noises, looked out, and saw a person with a flashlight working at the side door of the garage for about a minute before stepping inside. The homeowner called 911. Police arrived within six minutes and found {NAME} inside the garage, wearing gloves and holding a flashlight, next to a shelf with power tools. Nothing was missing.

{NAME} testified that {his} cat had escaped that evening and that {he} was searching nearby yards. {He} said {he} heard a noise inside the garage, found the side door unlocked, and stepped in to look for the cat. A "lost cat" post from {NAME} appeared on a local community app at 1:50 a.m. The cat was found two days later, three streets away.

The homeowner testified that the side door was locked earlier that night. Officers photographed fresh-looking scratches around the latch; a detective said they were consistent with a thin tool. No tool was found on {NAME}, and no older photos of the door exist for comparison.

calibracao: O notebook furtado estava na sala comum da casa do réu, e um inquilino sumiu; mas o histórico do notebook mostra o e-mail pessoal do réu aberto nele no dia seguinte ao furto, e o réu tinha uma janela de 50 min no almoço.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 26, a barista, is charged with residential burglary of a house from which a laptop, a tablet, and a set of headphones were stolen during the day.

The laptop had tracking software. Two days after the burglary, the owner located it at a house where {NAME} rents a room with three other tenants. Police found the laptop in a shared living room. Its browser history shows {NAME}'s personal email account being opened on it the day after the burglary. The tablet and headphones were not found.

One of the other tenants had moved out the day after the burglary and could not be located. {NAME} testified that this tenant brought the laptop home, said it had been "bought cheap from a friend," and let {NAME} use it once to check email. The remaining two tenants testified that they had never seen the laptop but rarely used the living room.

A neighbor of the burglarized house saw a person on a bicycle leave the house carrying a backpack. {NAME} owns a bicycle, as do the other tenants. Phone location data place {NAME} at work during most of the estimated burglary window, but there is a 50-minute gap during {his} lunch break; the house is about 10 minutes away by bicycle.

calibracao: Um vizinho viu o carteiro indo para os fundos da casa às 2:00, mas o réu ficou só 4 min no endereço; o GPS mostra que o veículo postal voltou à rua às 4:40, depois do fim da rota, e ficou parado 12 min; ninguém viu a entrada.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 31, a postal mail carrier, is charged with residential burglary of a house on {his} delivery route. Someone entered through an unlocked back door during the day and took a tablet, a laptop, and several pieces of jewelry.

A neighbor testified to seeing {NAME}, whom the neighbor recognized as the regular mail carrier, walking along the side of the house toward the backyard at about 2:00 p.m. Postal scan records show that {NAME} delivered a package to that house at 1:57 p.m., leaving it at the front door. The postal vehicle's GPS shows {him} at the next stop four minutes later.

The GPS also shows that, at 4:40 p.m., after {NAME}'s route had ended, the postal vehicle returned to the same street and stayed parked two houses away for 12 minutes. The homeowners left for work at 8:00 a.m. and returned at 6:30 p.m. A different neighbor saw a person in a gray sweatshirt in the backyard "sometime in the afternoon" but could not describe the face.

{NAME} testified that {he} walked toward the side gate at 2:00 p.m. only to look for a safer place to leave the package, and that {he} returned at 4:40 p.m. to eat a late lunch in a shaded spot {he} often uses.

calibracao: Vidro e fibras são provas de classe, e o réu tem explicação parcial para o vidro; o réu foi parado perto do local pouco depois do arrombamento.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 36, a freelance photographer, is charged with residential burglary of a house where a glass patio door was smashed and electronics worth about $4,000 were taken.

Police stopped {NAME} about one kilometer from the house, 50 minutes after a neighbor reported the sound of breaking glass. A lab found three tiny glass fragments on {NAME}'s jacket with the same refractive index as the patio door glass, a type used in millions of doors. Blue fibers on the broken door frame were consistent with {NAME}'s jacket, a mass-produced item.

{NAME} testified that {he} spent the evening at a friend's home helping repair a broken window, which explains the glass. The friend confirmed this and showed a receipt for window glass bought that afternoon, but an expert testified that the friend's window used a different type of glass. No stolen items were found on {NAME} or in {his} car. {NAME} has a conviction for burglary from 11 years ago.

calibracao: A confissão foi a um informante de cela, com benefício, que só repetiu detalhes já publicados na imprensa; o réu quitou um empréstimo em espécie duas semanas depois do furto.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 41, an insurance broker, is charged with residential burglary of a house from which a safe containing about $20,000 in cash and documents was removed. The owners were away for the weekend when it happened.

A person who shared a jail cell with {NAME} for three days, after {his} arrest on an unrelated traffic warrant, testified that {NAME} described "taking a safe out of a house on the lake road" and said it took two people to carry it. In exchange for testifying, the informant received a reduced sentence on a fraud charge. Those details had appeared in a local news article.

Investigators found that {NAME} paid off a $6,000 car loan in cash two weeks after the burglary. {NAME} testified that the money came from selling a boat and produced a handwritten bill of sale; the buyer could not be located. {NAME} denies ever talking about the burglary.

calibracao: Os pagamentos saíram do login do réu, cuja senha ficava num bilhete no computador compartilhado; mas quatro foram aprovados pelo acesso remoto a partir da casa do réu, e nenhum ocorreu nas duas semanas de férias do réu. Nenhum dinheiro foi rastreado até o réu.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 39, a staff accountant, is charged with embezzlement from the furniture company where {he} worked. Four of the payments were approved on days when {NAME} was working from home; the remote access logs show {NAME}'s account connected from {his} home internet address on those days. No payments were made during the two weeks {NAME} was on vacation, although the other two employees worked as usual.

{NAME} testified that {he} never approved those payments and that anyone in the office could have used {his} login, even remotely, once they knew the password. Investigators found no unusual deposits in {NAME}'s bank accounts. {He} had taken on a large personal loan the year before.

calibracao: O réu diz que os cheques eram reembolsos e bônus autorizados verbalmente por um sócio que morreu antes do julgamento; o total é quatro vezes as despesas comprovadas.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 44, an office operations manager, is charged with embezzlement from a small architecture firm. Over two years, {NAME} deposited 22 company checks, totaling $36,750, into {his} personal bank account. The firm has eight employees and an outside accountant who reviews the books once a year.

{NAME} admits making the deposits. {He} testified that one of the firm's two founding partners verbally authorized the checks as reimbursement for expenses {he} paid personally and as an informal bonus. {NAME} produced receipts for about $9,400 in business expenses. Two of the checks bear the deceased partner's signature; the others were signed with a signature stamp that {NAME} was allowed to use for routine bills.

The firm's bookkeeper testified that the deceased partner "was informal about money" and sometimes gave bonuses without recording them.

calibracao: O caixa era compartilhado e houve faltas depois da suspensão do réu; mas as faltas nos turnos do réu foram, em média, quatro vezes maiores que as outras, e só o réu tinha o código do cofre.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 26, a shift supervisor at a gas station convenience store, is charged with embezzlement of about $6,200 in cash over three months.

The store's records show cash shortages on 13 shifts. {NAME} supervised 9 of them, and those 9 shortages averaged $620. The 4 shortages on shifts {he} did not work averaged $150. On {NAME}'s shifts, two cashiers also had access to the registers, but the supervisor was the only person with the code to the safe where cash was dropped.

The camera above the safe shows {NAME} opening the safe 38 times during those shifts. The video shows {him} counting cash, but the angle does not show whether any was removed. After {NAME} was suspended, shortages stopped for six weeks and then occurred twice more, for $90 and $120.

A cashier testified to once seeing {NAME} put "a folded stack of bills" into a jacket pocket; {NAME} testified that it was {his} own tip money from a second job. {His} bank records show cash deposits of $100 to $200 most weeks during the period, which {he} says came from weekend work for a wedding photographer; {he} produced two payment messages from the photographer.

calibracao: O réu criou o funcionário fantasma e diz que cumpria ordem do gerente, que fez acordo para depor contra o réu; mas há um e-mail do réu pedindo que o "dispatcher" não aparecesse no organograma, que o réu atribui a um pedido de sigilo.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 35, an accounting systems analyst responsible for payroll processing, is charged with embezzlement from a regional trucking company. For 15 months, a person who never worked at the company received biweekly paychecks totaling $41,600, deposited into an account controlled by the company's operations manager.

An email from {NAME} to the operations manager, sent a week after the record was created, says: "Make sure the new dispatcher doesn't end up on the org chart." {NAME} testified that {he} wrote it because the manager had said the hire was confidential.

The operations manager was also charged and agreed to testify against {NAME} in exchange for a reduced sentence. The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 24, a customer service desk associate at a department store, is charged with embezzlement for processing refunds onto {his} own debit card. Over four months, 31 refunds totaling $5,860 were paid to a card in {NAME}'s name.

{NAME} admits that the refunds went to {his} card. {He} testified that some customers who had paid in cash wanted their refunds immediately, so {he} refunded those amounts to {his} own card and handed the customers cash from {his} wallet, because the store's cash refund process took too long. {He} said a former supervisor told {him} this was acceptable; the former supervisor denies it.

The store found returned merchandise logged for 6 of the 31 refunds. For the other 25, there is no record of returned items. Store video for three of those refunds shows no customer at the desk. The refunds stopped the day after managers announced an audit of the service desk.

{NAME} withdrew cash from ATMs on most of the days the refunds were processed, which the defense says is consistent with replacing the cash {he} gave to customers.

calibracao: O colega de casa vendeu as placas de vídeo e pode ter agido sozinho; o réu ajustou o estoque para esconder as perdas e diz que só fazia seu trabalho; as transferências do colega ao réu somam bem mais que a parte do aluguel, e o réu atribui a diferença a contas e a um empréstimo sem registro.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 31, an inventory analyst at an electronics distributor, is charged with embezzlement of company inventory. Over six months, 46 new graphics cards worth $27,000 disappeared from the warehouse, and inventory records were adjusted to hide the losses.

The adjustments were made under {NAME}'s user account, which {NAME} admits only {he} uses. An online seller account, shipping from {NAME}'s home address, sold 39 graphics cards of the same model during that period. The seller account was registered to {NAME}'s housemate, a forklift operator at the same warehouse. The housemate invoked the right to remain silent.

{NAME} testified that {he} made the adjustments because physical counts were lower than system counts, which was {his} job, and that {he} reported the losses. The warehouse manager confirms two emails from {NAME} about shortages, but says {NAME} described them as counting errors.

Payments from the seller account went to the housemate's bank account. During the six months, the housemate transferred $6,000 to {NAME}. {NAME}'s share of the rent is $650 per month, or $3,900 for the period. {NAME} says the rest covered shared bills and repaid a personal loan {he} had made to the housemate, which was never written down.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 47, a regional sales director at a medical equipment company, is charged with embezzlement for using a corporate credit card for personal purchases. An internal audit found $23,900 in charges over one year that the company classified as personal: weekend hotel stays, restaurant meals near {NAME}'s home, and electronics.

Two clients testified that {NAME} took them to dinner several times near {his} home but could not remember the dates.

The audit found that 11 weekend hotel stays were in a resort town where {NAME} has no clients; a conference was held there on only two of those weekends. The electronics, a laptop and two tablets, were not in the company's asset records; {NAME} testified that {he} used them for client presentations.

calibracao: O réu é vítima documentada de roubo de identidade e diz que não abriu a conta de pagamento; mas o login do réu mudou o destino das doações no dia em que a conta foi aberta, e parte do dinheiro pagou dívidas do réu.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 30, an operations coordinator at a nonprofit food bank, is charged with embezzlement of $18,400 in donations. Donations made through a campaign page that {NAME} managed were sent to a payment account opened in {NAME}'s name instead of the nonprofit's account.

{NAME} testified that {he} never opened the payment account and that {his} identity had been stolen. {He} had filed a police report about identity theft four months earlier, after someone opened a credit card in {his} name.

The campaign page's logs show that {NAME}'s staff login changed the page's payout destination to the new account on the same day that account was opened. The food bank's director testified that {NAME} was the only staff member who changed the page settings during the period. {NAME} said {he} did not remember making that change and that {his} login could have been stolen too.

Of the money, $6,000 paid off {NAME}'s overdue car loan and $3,200 went to {NAME}'s landlord. {NAME} testified that {he} did not notice those payments because {he} had set up automatic payments from several accounts. The rest was withdrawn in cash at ATMs in another city.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 37, a treasury analyst at a community credit union, is charged with embezzlement of $52,000. Over two years, small amounts were moved from dormant member accounts into an internal suspense account and then transferred to an outside account belonging to a company registered under a false name.

A spreadsheet tracking the dormant accounts and each transfer was found on {NAME}'s work computer. The transfers were made with two employee logins: {NAME}'s and that of a coworker who left the credit union a year earlier and could not be found.

After a three-hour meeting with the board and the credit union's lawyer, {NAME} wrote an email to the board: "I should have reported what was happening with the dormant accounts. I'm sorry for my part in this." {NAME} testified that {his} "part" was failing to report transfers {he} had noticed and that the spreadsheet was {his} own effort to track the problem.

The outside company's bank account was opened with a phone number that once belonged to the former coworker.

calibracao: O réu diz que acreditava num costume antigo de ficar com o dinheiro dos móveis excedentes, confirmado por um técnico; mas assinava todo ano um termo dizendo que esses móveis são da empresa, e não declarou a renda.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 43, a facilities coordinator at a commercial property company, is charged with embezzlement for selling the company's surplus office furniture and keeping the money. Over 18 months, {NAME} sold surplus furniture from building renovations to a used furniture dealer 17 times, receiving $14,700.

{NAME} admits the sales. {He} testified that a former facilities director told {him} years earlier that staff could "take care of the old furniture" and keep the proceeds, and that this had long been the practice. A maintenance technician who worked at the company for 12 years testified that the previous coordinator also sold surplus furniture and kept the money. The former director could not be located.

Each year, {NAME} signed an asset policy acknowledgment stating that "surplus furniture and equipment remain company property until disposed of through the facilities office." {NAME} testified that {he} signed it with other routine forms without reading it closely. {NAME} did not report the income on {his} tax returns and never mentioned the sales to the current director, who joined two years ago.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 29, a pharmacy manager, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a cyclist at about 11:20 p.m. on a two-lane road. The cyclist suffered a broken leg. A witness wrote down a partial plate and described a silver hatchback.

Police found {NAME}'s silver hatchback the next morning with a cracked headlight and a dent on the front right fender. Paint transfer from the bicycle matched the dent, and the plate matches the partial plate.

{NAME} shares the car with {his} housemate, and both have keys. {NAME} testified that {he} was asleep at home that night and that the housemate had borrowed the car. The housemate testified to returning the car at 9:30 p.m. and staying home afterward.

At 11:05 p.m., {NAME}'s credit card paid for fuel at a gas station three kilometers from the collision. The station's camera was not working. {NAME} testified that the housemate sometimes uses the card for gas with {his} permission; the housemate denies using it that night.

The witness saw the driver only from behind and could not describe the person. The car's seat position fit both people.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 52, a high school chemistry teacher, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a pedestrian at about 6:40 p.m. on a rainy winter evening. The pedestrian was walking at the edge of a narrow street without sidewalks, was struck by a side mirror, and fell into a ditch, suffering a broken wrist and a concussion.

{NAME} admits driving on that street at the time and admits feeling "a bump." {He} testified that {he} thought {he} had hit a pothole, which is common on that street, and kept driving home. The next morning, {NAME} reported the broken right side mirror to {his} insurer as pothole damage.

A neighbor who heard the impact testified that it was "a loud bang" and that the car did not slow down. It was raining hard, and {NAME} said the radio was on.

An accident reconstruction expert testified that a driver could have seen the pedestrian in the headlights for about two seconds before impact, but that after impact the pedestrian fell to the right, outside the driver's line of sight. The pedestrian was wearing dark clothing.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 34, a software tester, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a motorcyclist at an intersection at about 1:15 a.m. A traffic camera recorded a gray SUV running a red light, hitting the motorcycle, and driving away. The image shows the plate, registered to {NAME}, but not the driver.

At 7:40 a.m. the same morning, {NAME} reported the SUV stolen from the street outside {his} apartment. Police found the SUV two days later, abandoned in a parking lot about three kilometers from the collision, with front-end damage. The ignition had been forced with a tool. A detective testified that thieves usually force ignitions, but that owners covering up a crime sometimes damage their own cars.

Router records show that {NAME}'s phone disconnected from {his} home Wi-Fi at 12:40 a.m. and reconnected at 1:50 a.m. {NAME} testified that {he} was asleep and that the phone sometimes drops the connection overnight; the records show no other disconnection that week. {NAME}'s apartment is about 15 minutes from the intersection.

{NAME} has a prior conviction for driving under the influence from five years ago, which the prosecution offers as a motive to avoid another arrest.

calibracao: O reconhecimento foi feito numa audiência em que o réu era o único acusado, e o dano no carro pode vir de um poste; mas a localização do celular segue pela mesma rua até depois da faixa, contra "virei antes", com precisão de cerca de 300 m.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 27, a restaurant host, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a pedestrian in a crosswalk at about 9:50 p.m. The pedestrian suffered a fractured hip.

A bus driver waiting at the light testified to seeing the driver's face through the side window for "a second or two" as the car turned and drove off. The street lighting was poor. Days later, the bus driver saw {NAME} in the courtroom during a preliminary hearing, where {NAME} was the only person charged, and said, "That's the driver." The bus driver was never shown a photo lineup.

{NAME}'s blue sedan has a dent in the front bumper. A paint expert testified that the dent is consistent with hitting a person but could also have come from a low-speed impact with a pole. {NAME} testified that {he} hit a parking pole a week earlier.

Phone location data place {NAME}'s phone about 600 meters before the crosswalk at 9:44 p.m. and about 400 meters past it, on the same road, at 9:53 p.m. {NAME} testified that {he} turned off before the crosswalk and took a side street; an analyst testified that the location points are accurate only to about 300 meters.

calibracao: O réu sabia da batida, parou 70 s e foi embora sem trocar dados, dizendo que a outra pessoa o dispensou e não parecia ferida; o vídeo mostra a outra pessoa levando a mão ao pescoço, e o réu procurou a loja no dia seguinte.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 38, a hotel operations manager, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured another driver at about 5:30 p.m. in a supermarket parking lot exit.

The other driver testified that {NAME}'s car backed into the driver's door. {NAME} got out, looked at the damage, said something like "it's just a scratch," and drove away before the two exchanged information. Data from {NAME}'s car's event recorder show an impact at 5:31 p.m. at 9 km/h. The supermarket camera shows {NAME} standing next to the other car for about 70 seconds, then leaving. During that time, the other driver stays seated and, at least twice, holds a hand to the back of the neck. The video has no audio.

{NAME} testified that the other driver said "don't worry about it" and waved {him} off, and that {he} did not notice any sign of injury. The other driver denies saying that. {NAME} called the supermarket the next day to ask whether anyone had reported damage.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 33, a sales account manager, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a jogger on a rural road at about 6:15 a.m. The jogger suffered a broken arm and could not describe the car.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 36, a museum educator, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a pedestrian at about 12:40 a.m. The pedestrian suffered a broken pelvis.

A security camera recorded a dark gray sedan with a car-sharing company logo hitting the pedestrian and driving away. The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 31, a city planner, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a teenager riding an electric scooter at about 8:20 p.m. The rider suffered a broken ankle and remembers only a "gray car."

Phone location data place {NAME}'s phone on the same street at 8:19 p.m. {NAME} drives a gray compact car. At about 9:20 p.m., {NAME}'s phone searched for "what happens if you hit someone and drive away" and "how long do police keep traffic camera footage." The nearest traffic camera was not working that night.

Investigators found no damage on {NAME}'s car. A mechanic testified that a scooter could hit a car without leaving visible damage. The rider's scooter had a scrape of gray paint, too small to compare. At least 40 gray compact cars are registered within two kilometers of the scene.

{NAME} testified that {he} was driving home on that street but did not hit anyone, and that the searches were prompted by a true-crime podcast about a hit-and-run case. {NAME}'s podcast app shows that episode starting at 9:40 p.m., after the searches. {NAME} said {he} had heard an earlier episode of the same series that afternoon; the app shows no other episode played that day.
